statute_note: Principal source selected: the LankaLaw HTML consolidated edition (15-1876-matrimonial-rights-and-inheritance-ordinance-consolidated.html, page 1981Y4V69C-1 = Chapter 69 of the 1981 revised edition, volume 4), parsed into 15-1876-matrimonial-rights-and-inheritance-ordinance.json: 3 Parts, 36 sections, 4 definitions, no Schedule; already structurally_verified. Other sources inspected: the registry PDF statutes/15-1876-matrimonial-rights-and-inheritance-ordinance.pdf (LankaLaw, Cap. 69, 6 pp.), which the previous manifest called an image scan; it is a scan with an embedded OCR text layer of poor quality ('Nos'' for 'Nos.', '18 ol 1922', 'balf blood'), usable for the header block and for spot checks and carried as a verification source, not parsed. Consolidation cutoff: Ordinance No. 18 of 1923 on the HTML header ('Ordinance Nos, 15 of 1876 18 of 1923'); the PDF header reads 'Ordinances Nos' 15 of 1876 2 of 1889 18 ol 1922'. The two copies therefore disagree on the year of the last instrument (1923 vs 1922, a single-digit conflict on the same instrument in an OCR layer that misreads 'of' on the same line) and the HTML omits 2 of 1889, which the PDF lists. Neither copy carries an inline marker. Both copies date the Ordinance '29th June, 1877' at its head and both print the editorial note that sections 4 to 19 are repealed by section 4 of the Married Women's Property Ordinance for persons married on or after 29 June 1877; data/processed/statute_commencement.csv gives 1876-06-29, which the tree already records as wrong (commencement_correction). Review performed: header block, chain, head date and the sections 4-19 editorial note read in both copies; the tree's 36 section headings and node texts were run against the PDF text layer (8-word chunk matching) and spot-checked by eye; where the PDF layer is legible it agrees with the HTML, and the many non-matches are column interleaving and OCR noise in the PDF rather than different wording -- no substantive disagreement was found, but the check is limited by the PDF's quality and is recorded as spot-level, not line by line. Validator: zero errors; the one warning (section 14 keeps its text on the section node) is documented in the tree. Amendment coverage: two instruments, both known_but_not_held. 2 of 1889 (the Civil Procedure Code) from the PDF header only; 18 of 1923/1922 from both headers with the digit conflict. Nothing applied. The curriculum lists no amendments. OCR or structural weaknesses: the PDF's OCR layer; the 1922/1923 conflict; sections 4 to 19 are reproduced in full and not marked repealed node by node (flagged in the tree); section 19 carries the editor's note '(+ This section has no relevance today.)'. Missing sources: own text of both amending Ordinances; a printed revised edition to settle the year. Unresolved questions: the year of Ordinance No. 18 (1922 or 1923) and whether 2 of 1889 belongs in the chain. Lawyer-verification status: unverified. Everything here is pipeline output.
